Hiring is often preferred when time is limited, the skill gap is too large to close through training, or when a new hire brings a fresh perspective or unique experience. One point of interest in this study is that survey respondents identified keeping up with codes, technology, or certification, as a reason for training existing workers versus hiring new. This has potential implications for how training programs for different technologies or certifications can be marketed: outreach for training for new technologies or certifications may be more effective when focused on upskilling existing workers, whereas broader or more established programs such as traditional trades apprenticeships may be more appropriate to market to a broader audience of new entrants to the workforce. When responses were too vague about whether they were responding to hiring or training, they were omitted. Although the average reported value of 67% skewed toward more staff being well trained, the remaining gap indicates a clear need for additional training. What Makes a Worker Well Trained? Experience, quality, adaptability, communication, and attitude were reported as key characteristics that make a worker well trained. By thematically analyzing written responses from contractors, we identified key themes and their frequencies (see Table A-3 for codebook in Appendix A).
